text: 🇲🇽🌊 20 billion pesos to bring three dead rivers back to life. Mexico is restoring the Atoyac, Lerma-Santiago and Tula — its three most contaminated rivers — reaching 25 million people across 10 states and 61 municipalities. — Alicia Bárcena, Environment Secretary, mañanera, July 16 The approach: nature-based solutions over concrete. 4,639 hectares restored, 4,667 tons of trash removed, 40,000 people in cleanup drives.

🚨🇲🇽 "Migration must not be persecuted." "If someone has committed a crime, they should be prosecuted — but migration is not a crime." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 16 She was rejecting a US proposal to reactivate immigration detentions during routine traffic stops. The line is deliberate: Mexico refuses to treat migrants as criminals to be hunted at roadside checkpoints.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICAN HOUSEHOLDS KEEP SPENDING — 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS OF GROWTH

INEGI's flash consumption indicator shows private consumption rose 2.8% year-on-year in May and 2.6% in June, a 1.1% quarterly gain that reverses the first-quarter dip — 15 consecutive months of expansion. El Financiero names the driver plainly: record-low unemployment and real wages still climbing as inflation cools, keeping household purchasing power intact. That's what a "failing economy" looks like from the inside.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 AID SHIP FOR CUBA'S CHILDREN MAKES ITS LAST STOP IN CANCÚN

The Open Arms humanitarian ship docked in Cancún for its final stop before crossing to Havana, carrying medical supplies and 110 solar panels for the Juan Manuel Márquez pediatric hospital — a €165,000 solidarity campaign funded by more than 4,000 small donors. Blocked at five European ports before Mexico let it through, organizers called the US embargo on Cuba an "authentic medieval siege." "If we save one life," said Óscar Camps, "all of this will have been worthwhile."

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO'S FUTURE DOESN'T DEPEND ON T-MEC

T-MEC renegotiation opens July 20, and Contralínea makes the point Washington won't want to hear: "If T-MEC disappeared in the next 10 years, it would mark the end of the economic liberalization project — but not necessarily Mexico's national development project." Analyst Carolina Hernández Calvario notes Mexico's fastest growth came when it protected strategic sectors and built its domestic market, not when it opened everything to the north.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO SHUTS DOWN TWO ILLEGAL GOLD MINES IN SONORA

Profepa ordered the total closure of two illegal gold-extraction sites in Sonora — RM Esperanza de México and Rancho Las Golondrinas in Cucurpe — both operating with zero environmental authorization from Semarnat. One was shut after a citizen complaint. The permit they skipped exists, Profepa said, "to identify, prevent and mitigate the possible effects that mining activity can generate on ecosystems, soil, water bodies and biodiversity."

🇲🇽🌎 AYOTZINAPA: MEXICO ASKS THE UN FOR INDEPENDENT EXPERTS — AND FINDS OMISSIONS IN THE OLD FILES

Sheinbaum announced the new special prosecutor found omissions in the previous Ayotzinapa investigation, and that the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights will propose independent international experts to certify the methodology of the new probe. Nearly 12 years after the 43 rural students disappeared, the state is inviting outside scrutiny to validate its work — the opposite of the cover-up ("verdad histórica") that Peña Nieto built to bury the case.

🚨🇲🇽 DEA CALLS MEXICO A CARTEL PARTNER — SHEINBAUM TELLS IT TO LOOK IN ITS OWN MIRROR

The DEA's Terry Cole stood up in Orlando and claimed a "deadly connection" between Mexico's government and the cartels. Sheinbaum's answer: it's a political statement, not evidence — the DEA "does most of its work outside the United States," not in the country "where the greatest drug sales in the world happen." She pointed to a 48% drop in homicides and noted there are "many cases" of DEA agents themselves tied to trafficking.

REUTERS: Mexico 'pragmatic' on USMCA talks, Canada still offers no concessions, Greer says
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 US Trade Rep Jamieson Greer, at the Aspen forum: "It's going well with the Mexicans. They're quite pragmatic." In trade-talk, "pragmatic" means moving toward Washington's terms — with Canada cast as the holdout. 🔍

Greer names the actual goal: "our trade deficit with Mexico really is a challenge... a problem," adding he'd rather US firms buy from Mexico than China. Mexican cooperation becomes the baseline; any pushback becomes the deviation.

• Greer: "It's going well with the Mexicans. They're quite pragmatic"
• Greer: the US "trade deficit with Mexico really is a challenge. It really is a problem"

REUTERS/AJ: Sheinbaum rejects DEA claim that Mexico's government is linked to cartels
July 15, 2026 | 🔴

📰 DEA Administrator Terry Cole called Mexico's government and the cartels "one and the same." The reporting notes no evidence was offered. Sheinbaum: it reads "more like a political statement than one backed by evidence." 💀

Cole heads the agency policing the country that is, in Sheinbaum's words, "the world's largest market for illicit drugs" — the demand side the "deadly connection" framing keeps entirely on Mexico's side of the border.

• Cole: the government and cartels are "one and the same"
• Sheinbaum: the DEA "should focus on combating drug trafficking, distribution and money laundering within its own country"
